Question 2

#make the category
flights_with_time_cats <- flights %>%
  mutate(dep_category = case_when(
    dep_time >= 0 & dep_time < 600 ~ "early morning",
    dep_time >= 600 & dep_time < 1200 ~ "morning",
    dep_time >= 1200 & dep_time < 1800 ~ "afternoon",
    dep_time >= 1800 & dep_time <= 2400 ~ "evening"
  ),
  arr_category = case_when(
    arr_time >= 0 & arr_time < 600 ~ "early morning",
    arr_time >= 600 & arr_time < 1200 ~ "morning",
    arr_time >= 1200 & arr_time < 1800 ~ "afternoon",
    arr_time >= 1800 & arr_time <= 2400 ~ "evening"
  ))
#show the barplot
ggplot(flights_with_time_cats, aes(x = dep_category)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Flights by Departure Time Category",
       x = "Time of Day",
       y = "Number of Flights")
ggplot(flights_with_time_cats, aes(x = arr_category)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Flights by Arrival Time Category",
       x = "Time of Day",
       y = "Number of Flights")
#percentage
redeye_flights <- flights_with_time_cats %>%
  filter((dep_category == "afternoon" | dep_category == "evening") &
         (arr_category == "early morning" | arr_category == "morning")) %>%
  nrow()

total_flights <- flights_with_time_cats %>% nrow()

redeye_percentage <- (redeye_flights / total_flights) * 100

print(paste("The percentage of 'red eye' flights is:", redeye_percentage, "%"))
[1] "The percentage of 'red eye' flights is: 3.15729149345559 %"

What is the relationship: The two datasets can be joined by the origin column in the weather table, which corresponds to the faa airport code in the airports table. How it should appear in the diagram: There should be a line connecting the weather and airports data frames, specifically linking the weather.origin variable to the airports.faa variable. This indicates that weather.origin is a foreign key referring to the primary key airports.faa for the three NYC airports.

# Check for duplicates
num_duplicates <- sum(duplicated(weather_unique$weather_id))
print(paste("Number of duplicated values:", num_duplicates))
[1] "Number of duplicated values: 3"

There should be 0 duplicated value because after combined those 5 variables in one unit, each value is unique and there is no other value that can be the same to it. But the results is 3,the documentation for nycflights13 mentions a specific data entry error on November 3, 2013, at 1 AM, where some records were duplicated. This is why using year, month, day, hour, and origin does not result in a perfectly unique key。

Question 8

avg_delay_by_dest <- flights %>%
  group_by(dest) %>%
  summarise(avg_arr_delay = mean(arr_delay, na.rm = TRUE))

airports_with_delay <- airports %>%
  inner_join(avg_delay_by_dest, by = c("faa" = "dest"))
us_map <- map_data("state")

ggplot(us_map, aes(x = long, y = lat)) +
  geom_polygon(fill = "gray90", color = "gray60") +
  geom_point(data = airports_with_delay, aes(x = lon, y = lat, color = avg_arr_delay), alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "darkred", high = "blue", name = "Avg. Delay (min)") +
  coord_quickmap() +
  labs(title = "Spatial Distribution of Average Flight Delays by Destination")

Question 9 1.define “bad weather” and calculate the average delay in those conditions compared to “good weather”

bad_weather_flights <- merged_flights_weather %>%
  filter(precip > 0.05 | visib < 2 | wind_speed > 25)

good_weather_flights <- merged_flights_weather %>%
  filter(precip == 0 & visib >= 10 & wind_speed <= 10)

avg_delay_bad_weather <- mean(bad_weather_flights$dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE)

avg_delay_good_weather <- mean(good_weather_flights$dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("Average departure delay during bad weather:", round(avg_delay_bad_weather, 2), "minutes\n")
Average departure delay during bad weather: 28.6 minutes
cat("Average departure delay during good weather:", round(avg_delay_good_weather, 2), "minutes\n")
Average departure delay during good weather: 8.91 minutes

Comparison of average delays in “bad” vs. “good” weather is a strong indicator. The results show that avg_delay_bad_weather is significantly higher than avg_delay_good_weather, it suggests that bad weather(as defined) can have large impact on delays

2.The correlation matrix plot visually confirms which weather variables are most correlated with delays. A stronger positive correlation between a weather variable and dep_delay indicates a stronger impact.

library(corrplot)
corrplot 0.95 loaded
cor_matrix <- merged_flights_weather %>%
  select(dep_delay, temp, wind_speed, precip, visib) %>%
  cor(use = "complete.obs")

corrplot(cor_matrix, method = "circle", title = "Correlation Matrix of Delay and Weather", mar = c(0, 0, 1, 0))

The correlation matrix will provide a more precise measure of which weather variables have the strongest linear relationship with departure delays. Variables visib (visibility) show strongest negative correlation with dep_delay (lower visibility means higher delay), while variables precip(precipitation ) show strongest positive correlation.

3.This boxplot visualizes how the distribution of departure delays changes with different levels of precipitation(strongest correlation as previous plot said). It’s a good way to see if heavier rain is associated with a wider spread of delays or higher median delays.

# Categorize precipitation for plotting
merged_flights_weather %>%
  mutate(precip_cat = cut(precip, 
                          breaks = c(-0.1, 0.001, 0.1, 0.5, 100), 
                          labels = c("none", "light", "moderate", "heavy"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = precip_cat, y = dep_delay)) +
  geom_boxplot(na.rm = TRUE) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-20, 100)) + # Limit y-axis for better visualization
  labs(title = "Departure Delay by Precipitation Level",
       x = "Precipitation Level",
       y = "Departure Delay (minutes)")

It can be seen that the median have positive correlation to rain levels.And after level of moderate rain levels(50%),the range of delay remains almost the same, which means that the impact of precipitation level to delay gets weaken after certain extent.

4.scatter plot shows the relationship between wind speed and departure delays. It’s expected to show that as wind speed increases, the average delay tends to increase as well. The trendline helps to highlight this linear relationship.

ggplot(merged_flights_weather, aes(x = visib, y = dep_delay)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "darkblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = FALSE) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-30, 800), xlim = c(0, 11)) +
  labs(title = "Departure Delay vs. visible",
       x = "visible (mph)",
       y = "Departure Delay (minutes)")
